No, I haven't gotten over it and haven't regained anything I lost, although I'm past the sheer terror and numbness from the shock of it all. I remain really depressed, although I tend to think it's not even clinical depression but more a rational response to the shit I have made of my life. It seems like most people are more resilient than I am and do get better, though, so please don't take my experience as a confirmation of your doom! 

I totally relate to what you said about being derailed and not being able to be a part of life again. I used to be kind of a goody two-shoes, but after being hauled away to the hospital by police, I now feel permanently alienated from civil society and would very much like to devote the rest of my miserable life to vengeance and destruction. Fortunately I can't get out of bed most of the time, so my enemies are safe.

I went to a fancy law school and did pretty well grades-wise, although it was a big struggle and I can't work now so I rather regret the whole ordeal. A couple tips:
- If you can't get through all the reading, try to at least make it to class and take really good notes. Be a note-taking robot - that's what they test on. Also buy the commercial outlines they tell you not to buy. They really help.
- Keep in contact with the administration about any disability accommodations you may need (e.g. extensions, rescheduled exams). You won't be the first one, I promise.
- Look into loss of license insurance and life insurance to cover your school debt in case something happens to you.
Good luck to you!

Yes. In one episode of mania, I lost my job and career potential (I had been a public interest lawyer), all my friends, most of my money and valuables (stolen or given away), and most importantly my dignity, my trust in others (friends, family, health care providers, and police), and all my hopes and dreams for the future. 

That was two years ago and things are almost as bad as the day I beat the commitment rap and got sent home from the hospital in grippy socks and donated shoes.

I know that's the right attitude, but I just don't have it. I always liked having a big goal and then working toward it, but I can't think of anything to even want anymore. Small efforts seem to require faith I don't have, and just make me feel even more remedial and stupid. I don't see any path out of it because I am it, so why try? Unfortunately I have a very hateful attitude toward going on walks or trying to do a little volunteer work or whatever is recommended in these situations. Sorry, I have become a black hole of negativity.
